about.title: Fullerton Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Fullerton sits at the north edge of Orange County, and its roughly 140,000 residents earn a living in warehouses, hospitals, classrooms, kitchens, and construction sites, and behind the wheel on Harbor Boulevard, Euclid Street, Orangethorpe Avenue, and the southbound 57. When a shift ends in an injury, the road ahead is often less clear than people expect. Under California law, workers' compensation is normally your only remedy against your employer, and it pays regardless of who was at fault. But it stops there. If a subcontractor, a property owner, the maker of a defective machine, or another driver played a part in what happened, a separate injury claim against that third party may be possible alongside comp benefits. That distinction carries weight in a city where so many people drive for work: Fullerton recorded 734 injury collisions in 2025, with reported crashes tending to cluster on Friday evenings. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who can weigh both angles of your situation.

items.title: We look past the comp claim
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party such as a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker can support a separate claim. The attorney we connect you with can check whether one exists.

items.title: Deadlines are watched closely
items.desc: You have 30 days to report an injury to your employer, and any third-party claim generally carries a two-year filing window in California. Early attorney involvement helps keep both on track.

items.question: I was rear-ended on Harbor Boulevard while making deliveries for my employer. Is that just a workers' comp case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because you were working, workers' compensation would typically cover your medical care and part of your lost wages regardless of fault. But the other driver is a third party, so you may also have a separate injury claim against them. An attorney can review both paths together.

items.question: Can my Fullerton employer fire me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No. Retaliating against a worker for reporting an injury or filing a workers' compensation claim is illegal in California. If you are demoted, cut from the schedule, or let go after reporting, tell the attorney you are connected with right away.

items.question: How long do I have to report a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: You should report the injury to your employer within 30 days, and it is wise to do so in writing. A separate claim against a negligent third party generally has a two-year deadline from the date of injury. Waiting can weaken either claim, so reaching out early matters.
